title: Adventures with Don Quijote
summary: Review the characters, adventures and main themes of Miguel de Cervantes's famous novel.
keyIdeas: Don Quijote de la Mancha is a famous novel by Miguel de Cervantes that parodies tales of chivalry.
Don Quijote often represents ideals and justice, while Sancho Panza offers practical thinking, common sense and popular wisdom.
The novel combines humour with ideas about friendship, freedom and the contrast between imagination and everyday reality.

activities.prompt: Aisha organises the classics section of the school library. Who wrote Don Quijote de la Mancha, and when was its first part published?
activities.explanation: Miguel de Cervantes published the first part, El ingenioso hidalgo don Quijote de la Mancha, in 1605, during Spain's Golden Age.
activities.hint: He is one of the best-known Spanish writers of the Golden Age.
options: Miguel de Cervantes Saavedra, in the early 17th century (1605)
Federico García Lorca, in the early 20th century
Félix Lope de Vega, in the late 18th century

activities.prompt: In the novel, Alonso Quijano loses touch with reality and decides to become a knight-errant because of his passion for tales of chivalry.
activities.explanation: True within the story: Alonso Quijano confuses chivalric fiction with reality. This is a fictional device, not a real consequence of reading a lot.

activities.prompt: Match each character or element to its description.
activities.explanation: These figures accompany or inspire Don Quijote on his journeys through La Mancha.

pairs.right: The loyal farmer and squire who travels on a donkey
The idealised lady to whom the knight dedicates his achievements
The donkey ridden by Sancho Panza

activities.prompt: Complete the Spanish sentence about a famous adventure in the novel.
activities.explanation: Don Quijote sees giants where there are windmills and mistakes their sails for arms. The chapter does not identify a specific town as the location.
activities.sentence: Don Quijote confunde los molinos de viento con temibles ___ de largos brazos a los que decide desafiar en combate.
options: hechiceros
dragones
gigantes

activities.prompt: Sort these traits and story details by whether they describe Don Quijote or Sancho Panza.
activities.explanation: Their outlooks complement each other: Don Quijote's dreaming idealism contrasts with Sancho's practical thinking.

items.text: Follows noble ideals, honour and fantasy
Uses popular sayings and hopes for practical rewards, such as an island to govern
Mistakes humble roadside inns for grand castles
Warns his master about reality using common sense
Rides a thin, old horse called Rocinante
Travels on a donkey he cares for affectionately

activities.prompt: Adrián summarises the windmill episode in Spanish. Put the events in order.
activities.explanation: Don Quijote sees the windmills, ignores Sancho's warning, attacks, falls and then blames an enemy enchanter.
items: Don Quijote divisa los molinos de viento en el campo y cree que son gigantes malvados.
Sancho Panza le advierte de que solo son molinos con aspas que mueve el viento.
Don Quijote se encomienda a su amada Dulcinea y embiste al primer molino a galope.
El viento mueve el aspa con fuerza, rompe la lanza y derriba al caballero y a Rocinante.
Don Quijote afirma que el sabio Frestón ha transformado los gigantes en molinos para quitarle la victoria.

activities.prompt: Hugo writes three statements about Don Quijote for a display. Which one contains a mistake about the story?
activities.explanation: An innkeeper at a humble inn makes Don Quijote a knight in a comic ceremony. Don Quijote imagines that the inn is a castle.
activities.hint: Who makes him a knight, and where does it happen?
options: Don Quijote mistakes flocks of sheep for two powerful armies fighting a battle.
Sancho Panza joins Don Quijote hoping to become governor of an island.
The king of Spain formally makes Don Quijote a knight in a grand royal palace.

activities.prompt: Read the Spanish text about Don Quijote's journey and answer the questions.
activities.explanation: The text describes Don Quijote's aims and the beginnings of his friendship with Sancho Panza.
activities.title: El ideal de Don Quijote
activities.text: En un rincón de La Mancha, Alonso Quijano pasaba los días y las noches sumergido en relatos de caballeros andantes, princesas encantadas y batallas heroicas. Tanto leyó que su imaginación transformó su modesta realidad. Decidió limpiar unas viejas armas oxidadas de sus bisabuelos, montar a su flaco rocín y salir a los caminos bajo el nombre de Don Quijote de la Mancha. Su propósito no era enriquecerse con dinero ni conquistar tierras para sí mismo, sino defender a los indefensos, enderezar entuertos y lograr que el mundo fuera un lugar más noble y justo. Aunque en su aldea pensaban que había perdido la cabeza, Don Quijote emprendió su viaje guiado por un ideal inquebrantable. A su lado marchaba Sancho, un vecino bondadoso que, pese a dudar de sus visiones, aprendió a admirar la generosidad y el gran corazón de su señor.

questions.prompt: What is Don Quijote's main aim when he sets out as a knight-errant?
questions.explanation: The text says he wants to protect those in need and make the world more just, rather than become rich.
options: To protect the defenceless and seek justice.
To gain riches and collect gold for his family.
To buy new land in La Mancha.

questions.prompt: What can we infer about Sancho's relationship with Don Quijote?
questions.explanation: Although Sancho doubts his master's fantasies, he comes to admire his generosity and kindness.
options: Sancho only follows him to laugh at him.
Despite Don Quijote's confused view of reality, Sancho values his kindness and noble spirit.
Sancho believes the inns are castles with drawbridges.

questions.prompt: Which value does this portrayal of Don Quijote offer readers today?
questions.explanation: This portrayal values noble dreams and the pursuit of justice despite difficulties.
options: Working towards noble and just ideals can be valuable even when reality makes it difficult.
People should not read books because books confuse them.
The only important thing in life is collecting possessions.

activities.prompt: Martina and Omar discuss Cervantes's purpose in their reading club. Which literary approach is central to the novel?
activities.explanation: Cervantes uses parody and irony to make a humorous criticism of the exaggerations in tales of chivalry.
activities.hint: Think about humorous imitation of medieval heroes.
options: Humorous parody of the exaggerated tales of chivalry of the time.
Tragic drama to frighten readers about travelling on roads.
A medieval fairy tale praising the magical powers of enchanters.

activities.prompt: Complete the meaning of this Spanish expression inspired by the novel.
activities.explanation: The expression refers to Don Quijote's mistake and can describe futile struggles against imaginary opponents or problems.
activities.sentence: Cuando decimos que alguien 'lucha contra molinos de viento', significa que se enfrenta a ___ que no existen en la realidad o que no puede vencer.
options: dificultades muy sencillas
enemigos o problemas imaginarios
personas justas y amables
